title: On to What’s Next . . .
coreMove: Mental quiet is only the first gate; before you trust it, ask what it will serve and require one visible proof in conduct, an apology, a duty, or a restraint.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a polished quiet mind may serve vanity unless the next act is tested
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one mentor conversation uses Seneca, Stoicism, Rome, and Nero to reframe calm as a conduct test

exampleSpecs.stakes: a student may turn a teaching on steadiness into permission to avoid duty
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a learner's confusion about the Bhagavad Gita, Arjuna, samatvam, and India becomes the lesson

exampleSpecs.audience: readers using quiet as a focus hack
exampleSpecs.stakes: the same practice can either polish ego or test motive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: parallel before and after halves use Seneca, Stoicism, Rome, and Nero to show the change

exampleSpecs.audience: readers checking whether quiet has changed action
exampleSpecs.stakes: the telling detail may be the duty that never appears in the record
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: reviewing records reveals a missed duty through Bhagavad Gita, Arjuna, samatvam, and India

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who hide resentment behind calm
exampleSpecs.stakes: inner quiet may become cover for the old resentment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: internal thought uses Seneca, Stoicism, Rome, and Nero without external dialogue

exampleSpecs.audience: readers assigning scarce attention before action
exampleSpecs.stakes: limited quiet time can feed self-image or prepare one responsible act
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: planning time uses Bhagavad Gita, Arjuna, samatvam, and India before any execution happens
